title: Move It, Mark It, Read the Result

scenes.tts: Look at a normal embryo and you cannot tell whether a tissue's fate is fixed or instructed by its neighbours. You cannot tell what a region sends, or what it can receive. So move the tissue. Put it in a new place, a new time or a new host, and read what it does.
scenes.narration: Look at a normal embryo and you cannot tell whether a tissue's fate is fixed or instructed by its neighbours. You cannot tell what a region sends, or what it can receive. So move the tissue. Put it in a new place, a new time or a new host, and read what it does.

scenes.tts: Pick a donor region and a host embryo. Donor and host can be the same stage, or different ages. The piece can go back to its own place, or to a new one. Shpay-mahn devised thin glass needles and wax plates with tiny wells to hold the egg still.

scenes.tts: Donor and host must be told apart. A graft looks like its host, so a second axis might simply be the graft growing according to its origin. Shpay-mahn and Mang-gold used newt species that differed in pigmentation. For birds, Luh Dwa-ran's marker is natural. Quail nuclei carry a large block of condensed chromatin that chick nuclei lack. The mark does not fade as cells divide.

scenes.tts: Let the host develop, then fix and section it. Pigmented cells in the new structure are host cells that were induced. Pale cells are donor cells. For birds, graft a short piece of quail neural tube into a chick embryo at the same axial level. Quail cells that emigrate can be recognised in sections long afterwards.

scenes.tts: A structure made of host cells shows instruction. A structure made of donor cells shows self-differentiation. The marker decides which. In this idealised example, one hundred twenty of twelve hundred neural tube cells are unpigmented. That is about ten percent donor, so about ninety percent host cells were induced. Of three hundred ten notochord cells, three hundred are unpigmented: about ninety-seven percent donor.
scenes.caption: A structure made of host cells shows instruction. A structure made of donor cells shows self-differentiation. The marker decides which. In this idealised example, 120 of 1,200 neural tube cells are unpigmented. That is about 10% donor, so about 90% host cells were induced. Of 310 notochord cells, 300 are unpigmented: about 97% donor.

scenes.tts: A graft is also a wound, so wound effects need a control. A natural pigment is not shared evenly by every descendant, so an injected dye can be used instead. Grafting itself may make artefacts. In Xenopus neural crest mapping, the team repeated the result with three methods. One injected a fluorescent dex-tran into a single blastomere, to label crest without grafting.

scenes.tts: In 1924, Shpay-mahn and Mang-gold reported grafting a small piece of dorsal lip from a pale newt gastrula into a pigmented one. A second body axis formed, and most of its neural tube was host tissue. From the early 1970s, Luh Dwa-ran and colleagues made quail chick chimeras. The permanent nuclear mark followed cells that left the graft, and mapped which level of the neural tube gives, for example, the face skeleton, ganglia, adrenal medulla and gut neurons.

scenes.tts: In 1976, Hollyday and Hamburger grafted an extra leg onto chick embryos. More motor neurons survived, but day six counts, before the normal loss, showed no extra. In cases selected for vigorous motility, the gain was eleven point zero to twenty-seven point five percent. The graft changed target size without touching the cord. A graft shows what a tissue does in a new place, and the marker says whose cells did it.
